questions.q: True or false? As the right ala, you should only watch the dribbler.
questions.explain: Right, it's false. You check the runner across goal and the ball, so nobody scores at the far post.
choiceExplanations: If you only watch the dribbler, the runner across goal is free for an easy tap-in.
Right, it's false. You check the runner across goal and the ball, so nobody scores at the far post.

questions.q: Blue switched the ball to the right. What should happen next?
options: Both alas run to the new ball carrier
The left ala recovers with the far runner
The right ala runs back to the far post
questions.explain: Yes. After a switch the jobs flip, so the left ala now tracks the far-post runner.
choiceExplanations: If both alas chase the ball, the runner at the new far post is left free.
Yes. After a switch the jobs flip, so the left ala now tracks the far-post runner.
The right ala is now on the ball side. They should move toward the ball and slow it.

questions.q: Blue has the ball on the right. Where should the left ala defend the far runner?
options: Into the middle, toward the ball
Up the court, away from our goal
questions.explain: Yes. Between the runner and our goal, the left ala can reach any pass across the box.
choiceExplanations: The fixo already guards the middle. Joining the ball leaves the far runner alone.
That space is behind the runner. They can get to our goal first.
Yes. Between the runner and our goal, the left ala can reach any pass across the box.
